barcelona.name: Barcelona
barcelona.note: Ildefons Cerdà's 1859 Eixample: a grid of octagonal blocks with chamfered corners, cut by the diagonal Avinguda Diagonal.

paris.name: Paris
paris.note: Haussmann's boulevards radiate from the Place de l'Étoile, the twelve-avenue star around the Arc de Triomphe.

amsterdam.name: Amsterdam
amsterdam.note: The 17th-century canal ring (Grachtengordel): concentric half-moon canals around the medieval core.

venice.name: Venice
venice.note: A city of canals and alleys on 118 islands, with the Grand Canal winding through in a reverse S.

london.name: London
london.note: Medieval street patterns survived the Great Fire; the Thames bends past Westminster and the Strand.

rome.name: Rome
rome.note: The twisting streets of the Campo Marzio sit inside a loop of the Tiber, with Via del Corso running dead straight.

vienna.name: Vienna
vienna.note: The Ringstraße replaced the city walls in the 1860s, wrapping the old Innere Stadt in a broad boulevard.

moscow.name: Moscow
moscow.note: Rings and radials spread out from the Kremlin's triangle on the Moskva river.

stpetersburg.name: Saint Petersburg
stpetersburg.note: A planned 18th-century capital: three avenues fan out from the Admiralty, crossed by canals.

berlin.name: Berlin
berlin.note: Unter den Linden runs from the Brandenburg Gate to Museum Island on the Spree, with the Friedrichstadt grid to the south.

madrid.name: Madrid
madrid.note: Streets converge on the Puerta del Sol, the city's Kilometre Zero, with the Gran Vía slicing through.

lisbon.name: Lisbon
lisbon.note: After the 1755 earthquake the Baixa was rebuilt as a strict grid, between tangled hillside districts on the Tagus.

prague.name: Prague
prague.note: The Charles Bridge crosses the Vltava between the Old Town and the Lesser Town below the castle.

budapest.name: Budapest
budapest.note: Buda and Pest face each other across the Danube, Pest's ring boulevards against Buda's castle hill.

istanbul.name: Istanbul
istanbul.note: The historic peninsula, bounded by the Golden Horn, the Bosphorus and the Sea of Marmara.

athens.name: Athens
athens.note: The 1830s neoclassical plan meets the old Plaka below the Acropolis.

copenhagen.name: Copenhagen
copenhagen.note: Old Copenhagen, the harbour, and the star-shaped bastions of Christianshavn.

stockholm.name: Stockholm
stockholm.note: Gamla stan's medieval island sits where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic.

edinburgh.name: Edinburgh
edinburgh.note: The medieval Old Town's spine faces James Craig's Georgian New Town grid across Princes Street Gardens.

dublin.name: Dublin
dublin.note: The quays line the River Liffey, with Georgian squares to the south-east.

brussels.name: Brussels
brussels.note: The old centre around the Grand-Place is enclosed by the Small Ring, a pentagon on the line of the old walls.

milan.name: Milan
milan.note: Concentric rings of boulevards follow the old walls around the Duomo.

florence.name: Florence
florence.note: The Roman grid survives around the Duomo; the Ponte Vecchio crosses the Arno.

naples.name: Naples
naples.note: The Greek grid of the centro storico is split by the long straight Spaccanapoli.

seville.name: Seville
seville.note: One of Europe's largest medieval old towns, a maze beside the Guadalquivir.

krakow.name: Kraków
krakow.note: The Planty park rings the Old Town where the walls once stood, around a huge market square.

warsaw.name: Warsaw
warsaw.note: Broad post-war avenues around the Palace of Culture and Science.

zurich.name: Zürich
zurich.note: The Limmat flows out of Lake Zürich between the medieval old town's two halves.

munich.name: Munich
munich.note: The Altstadtring loops around the old centre and the Marienplatz.

hamburg.name: Hamburg
hamburg.note: The Alster lakes, the old town's canals and the warehouse district on the Elbe.

oslo.name: Oslo
oslo.note: Kvadraturen, a Renaissance grid laid out by Christian IV in 1624, beside the fjord.

helsinki.name: Helsinki
helsinki.note: A neoclassical grid on a peninsula of bays and islands.

valletta.name: Valletta
valletta.note: A 1566 grid on a fortified peninsula between two deep harbours.

bordeaux.name: Bordeaux
bordeaux.note: The crescent-shaped Port of the Moon follows a bend of the Garonne.

lyon.name: Lyon
lyon.note: The Presqu'île between the Rhône and the Saône.

marseille.name: Marseille
marseille.note: Streets climb from the Vieux-Port, a natural harbour used for 2,600 years.

porto.name: Porto
porto.note: The steep Ribeira district drops to the Douro's gorge.

belgrade.name: Belgrade
belgrade.note: A ridge between the Sava and the Danube, ending at the Kalemegdan fortress.

bucharest.name: Bucharest
bucharest.note: Ceaușescu's Boulevard of the Victory of Socialism, ploughed through the old city to the Palace of the Parliament.

kyiv.name: Kyiv
kyiv.note: The Khreshchatyk boulevard runs along a valley below hills rising to the Dnipro.

riga.name: Riga
riga.note: The old town is ringed by a canal and boulevards on the line of its old walls, beside the Daugava.

glasgow.name: Glasgow
glasgow.note: A Victorian grid climbs the drumlins north of the Clyde.

reykjavik.name: Reykjavík
reykjavik.note: The small old centre sits between the harbour and the Tjörnin pond.

turin.name: Turin
turin.note: The Roman castrum grid of Augusta Taurinorum still shapes the arcaded centre.

valencia.name: Valencia
valencia.note: The old river Turia was turned into a sunken park that curves around the old town.

newyork.name: New York
newyork.note: The 1811 Commissioners' Plan: long narrow blocks, with Broadway cutting across on its old diagonal.

washington.name: Washington
washington.note: L'Enfant's 1791 plan lays diagonal avenues over a grid, meeting at circles and squares.

chicago.name: Chicago
chicago.note: The Loop: a dense grid hemmed in by the Chicago River and Lake Michigan.

sanfrancisco.name: San Francisco
sanfrancisco.note: Two grids meet at an angle along Market Street, laid over steep hills by the bay.

losangeles.name: Los Angeles
losangeles.note: Downtown's grid is tilted to the old Spanish pueblo, wrapped by freeways.

boston.name: Boston
boston.note: Crooked colonial streets around the Common, unlike most American cities.

philadelphia.name: Philadelphia
philadelphia.note: William Penn's 1682 grid between two rivers, with City Hall in its central square.

saltlakecity.name: Salt Lake City
saltlakecity.note: Mormon-plan blocks ten acres in size with extremely wide streets.

savannah.name: Savannah
savannah.note: Oglethorpe's 1733 plan of wards, each built around a small green square.

neworleans.name: New Orleans
neworleans.note: The French Quarter grid sits in a crescent bend of the Mississippi.

detroit.name: Detroit
detroit.note: Augustus Woodward's 1807 plan of radial avenues spreading from the riverfront.

seattle.name: Seattle
seattle.note: Downtown grids collide at angles on a hill between Elliott Bay and the I-5 trench.

toronto.name: Toronto
toronto.note: A grid by Lake Ontario, with the Toronto Islands offshore.

montreal.name: Montreal
montreal.note: Downtown sits between Mount Royal and the St. Lawrence, on a grid tilted from true north.

vancouver.name: Vancouver
vancouver.note: A peninsula between Burrard Inlet and False Creek, its grids skewed against each other.

mexicocity.name: Mexico City
mexicocity.note: The Zócalo and the colonial grid laid over the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan.

havana.name: Havana
havana.note: Old Havana packs a dense grid beside the harbour, with the Malecón seafront to the north.

miami.name: Miami
miami.note: Downtown on Biscayne Bay, with causeways and man-made islands offshore.

houston.name: Houston
houston.note: A tilted downtown grid inside a tight loop of freeways, by Buffalo Bayou.

denver.name: Denver
denver.note: Downtown's grid runs parallel to Cherry Creek, clashing with the compass grid around it.

indianapolis.name: Indianapolis
indianapolis.note: Alexander Ralston's Mile Square: four diagonal avenues meet at Monument Circle.

quebec.name: Quebec City
quebec.note: The walled upper town and the star-shaped Citadelle above the St. Lawrence.

austin.name: Austin
austin.note: Edwin Waller's 1839 grid runs from the Capitol down to the Colorado River.

guadalajara.name: Guadalajara
guadalajara.note: A colonial grid around the cathedral, with plazas arranged in a cross.

buenosaires.name: Buenos Aires
buenosaires.note: The Spanish manzana grid, cut by the Avenida de Mayo and the enormous Avenida 9 de Julio.

laplata.name: La Plata
laplata.note: Planned in 1882: a square grid crossed by diagonals, with a plaza every six blocks.

brasilia.name: Brasília
brasilia.note: Lúcio Costa's Pilot Plan: the Monumental Axis crossed by curving highways, without street corners.

rio.name: Rio de Janeiro
rio.note: Copacabana's narrow strip of streets between the beach and steep granite hills.

saopaulo.name: São Paulo
saopaulo.note: An old centre on a hill, wrapped in viaducts and expressways.

lima.name: Lima
lima.note: Pizarro's 1535 grid by the Rímac river, around the Plaza Mayor.

bogota.name: Bogotá
bogota.note: La Candelaria's colonial grid runs up to the steep wall of the eastern Andes.

santiago.name: Santiago
santiago.note: A colonial grid between the Mapocho river and Santa Lucía hill.

montevideo.name: Montevideo
montevideo.note: The Ciudad Vieja fills the tip of a peninsula in the Río de la Plata.

cusco.name: Cusco
cusco.note: The Inca capital, its streets running between Inca walls, folded into a mountain valley.

quito.name: Quito
quito.note: A colonial grid bent over the ravines and ridges of an Andean valley.

caracas.name: Caracas
caracas.note: A colonial grid squeezed into a long valley below Mount Ávila.

cartagena.name: Cartagena
cartagena.note: A walled colonial city on the Caribbean, surrounded by lagoons.

cairo.name: Cairo
cairo.note: The 19th-century downtown of radiating streets, beside the Nile and Gezira island.

marrakesh.name: Marrakesh
marrakesh.note: The walled medina's alleys and cul-de-sacs around Jemaa el-Fnaa square.

fez.name: Fez
fez.note: Fes el Bali, one of the largest car-free urban areas in the world: thousands of alleys in a valley.

casablanca.name: Casablanca
casablanca.note: Henri Prost's French colonial boulevards fan out beside the old medina and the port.

tunis.name: Tunis
tunis.note: The medina's maze meets the straight French Avenue Habib Bourguiba, running to the lake.

algiers.name: Algiers
algiers.note: The Casbah climbs a steep hillside above a French colonial seafront.

lagos.name: Lagos
lagos.note: Lagos Island, its old dense core ringed by lagoon, bridges and expressways.

nairobi.name: Nairobi
nairobi.note: A compact colonial grid by the railway, wrapped in highways.

capetown.name: Cape Town
capetown.note: A Dutch colonial grid between Table Bay and the slopes of Table Mountain.

johannesburg.name: Johannesburg
johannesburg.note: A gold-rush grid of tiny blocks, laid out quickly in 1886.

addisababa.name: Addis Ababa
addisababa.note: Roads wind across hills and stream valleys rather than following a grid.

dakar.name: Dakar
dakar.note: The Plateau, a colonial grid at the southern tip of the Cap-Vert peninsula.

accra.name: Accra
accra.note: The old core of Jamestown and Ussher Town on the Gulf of Guinea coast.

asmara.name: Asmara
asmara.note: A modernist colonial city of the 1930s, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

alexandria.name: Alexandria
alexandria.note: The Corniche sweeps around the Eastern Harbour of the city founded by Alexander.

zanzibar.name: Zanzibar City
zanzibar.note: Stone Town's narrow lanes fill a small triangular point on the Indian Ocean.

khartoum.name: Khartoum
khartoum.note: Kitchener's plan put diagonal streets over the grid, said to trace the Union Jack, by the Blue Nile.

dubai.name: Dubai
dubai.note: Deira and Bur Dubai, the old trading town, face each other across Dubai Creek.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: The walled Old City, its four quarters divided by the old Roman cardo and decumanus.

tehran.name: Tehran
tehran.note: A dense grid of avenues around the old bazaar and the Golestan Palace.

telaviv.name: Tel Aviv
telaviv.note: Patrick Geddes's 1925 plan of boulevards and garden blocks along the Mediterranean.

beirut.name: Beirut
beirut.note: The rebuilt downtown on a headland in the Mediterranean, with the port to the east.

tokyo.name: Tokyo
tokyo.note: The Imperial Palace moat meets the grids of Marunouchi and Ginza.

kyoto.name: Kyoto
kyoto.note: The checkerboard of the Heian capital, modelled on Chang'an in 794.

osaka.name: Osaka
osaka.note: The merchant city's grid crossed by rivers and canals, the 'Venice of the East'.

sapporo.name: Sapporo
sapporo.note: An American-advised grid of 1869, numbered by blocks, split by the long Ōdōri Park.

seoul.name: Seoul
seoul.note: Joseon palaces and the Cheonggyecheon stream at the heart of the old walled capital.

beijing.name: Beijing
beijing.note: A city on a north–south axis through the Forbidden City and Tiananmen Square.

shanghai.name: Shanghai
shanghai.note: The Bund and the old settlements on a bend of the Huangpu, facing Pudong.

hongkong.name: Hong Kong
hongkong.note: Central and Victoria Harbour: a narrow shelf of reclaimed land below steep hills.

taipei.name: Taipei
taipei.note: The Japanese-era grid on the site of the old walled city.

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.note: The Singapore River, the colonial core and the reclaimed land of Marina Bay.

bangkok.name: Bangkok
bangkok.note: Rattanakosin Island, ringed by canals and the Chao Phraya river.

hanoi.name: Hanoi
hanoi.note: The Old Quarter's guild streets next to Hoàn Kiếm Lake, near the Red River.

hochiminh.name: Ho Chi Minh City
hochiminh.note: French colonial boulevards of old Saigon, by the Saigon River.

manila.name: Manila
manila.note: The walled Spanish Intramuros by the mouth of the Pasig river on Manila Bay.

jakarta.name: Jakarta
jakarta.note: The great Medan Merdeka square and the National Monument, ringed by avenues.

yogyakarta.name: Yogyakarta
yogyakarta.note: The walled Kraton palace complex, on a north–south axis between Mount Merapi and the sea.

kualalumpur.name: Kuala Lumpur
kualalumpur.note: The old town grew where the Klang and Gombak rivers meet.

newdelhi.name: New Delhi
newdelhi.note: Lutyens's imperial capital of hexagons and roundabouts, centred on the Rajpath axis and Connaught Place.

mumbai.name: Mumbai
mumbai.note: The Fort district and the Oval Maidan at the southern tip of the island city.

kolkata.name: Kolkata
kolkata.note: BBD Bagh, the colonial core, on the Hooghly near the Howrah Bridge.

jaipur.name: Jaipur
jaipur.note: The 1727 walled Pink City, laid out in a grid of large rectangular blocks.

chandigarh.name: Chandigarh
chandigarh.note: Le Corbusier's sector plan: self-contained superblocks between fast roads.

kathmandu.name: Kathmandu
kathmandu.note: Medieval lanes and courtyards around Durbar Square.

karachi.name: Karachi
karachi.note: Colonial Saddar and the old town by the harbour and creeks.

lahore.name: Lahore
lahore.note: The walled old city, the Badshahi Mosque and the fort, ringed by gardens.

dhaka.name: Dhaka
dhaka.note: Old Dhaka's dense lanes run down to the Buriganga river.

colombo.name: Colombo
colombo.note: The Fort and Pettah districts by the harbour, with Beira Lake inland.

samarkand.name: Samarkand
samarkand.note: The Registan and old town, with a Russian colonial grid of tree-lined avenues to the west.

almaty.name: Almaty
almaty.note: A Russian colonial grid sloping up toward the Tian Shan mountains.

ulaanbaatar.name: Ulaanbaatar
ulaanbaatar.note: Soviet-era avenues around Sükhbaatar Square, ringed by ger districts.

pyongyang.name: Pyongyang
pyongyang.note: A monumental post-war capital of wide axes along the Taedong river.

sydney.name: Sydney
sydney.note: The CBD runs north to Circular Quay on a harbour of many coves.

melbourne.name: Melbourne
melbourne.note: Robert Hoddle's 1837 grid of wide streets and narrow lanes on the Yarra.

adelaide.name: Adelaide
adelaide.note: Colonel Light's Square Mile with five squares, entirely surrounded by parkland.

canberra.name: Canberra
canberra.note: Walter and Marion Griffin's plan of axes and circles around Lake Burley Griffin.

perth.name: Perth
perth.note: The CBD on the wide Swan River, beside Kings Park.

auckland.name: Auckland
auckland.note: Queen Street runs down a valley to the Waitematā Harbour.

wellington.name: Wellington
wellington.note: Streets squeezed between a harbour and steep hills, much of it on reclaimed land.

christchurch.name: Christchurch
christchurch.note: A grid inside the Four Avenues, with the Avon River winding through it.

brisbane.name: Brisbane
brisbane.note: The CBD fills a tight loop of the Brisbane River.

honolulu.name: Honolulu
honolulu.note: Waikīkī, a strip of hotels between the Ala Wai Canal and the Pacific.

varanasi.name: Varanasi
varanasi.note: Lanes too narrow for cars run down to the ghats, the stone steps along the Ganges, in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

chennai.name: Chennai
chennai.note: George Town grew as the 'Black Town' grid behind Fort St George, the East India Company's first fortress in India.

bengaluru.name: Bengaluru
bengaluru.note: The pete, the old market town of 1537, is a dense web of trade streets beside the later British cantonment.

hyderabad.name: Hyderabad
hyderabad.note: The Charminar, built in 1591, stands where four great roads of the Qutb Shahi city meet.

ahmedabad.name: Ahmedabad
ahmedabad.note: The walled city is made of pols: gated neighbourhoods of houses around winding dead-end lanes.

udaipur.name: Udaipur
udaipur.note: The City Palace and the old town line the shore of Lake Pichola, an artificial lake from the 14th century.

amritsar.name: Amritsar
amritsar.note: The walled city's bazaars and katras crowd around the Golden Temple and its sacred tank.

madurai.name: Madurai
madurai.note: Streets run in concentric squares around the Meenakshi temple, laid out like a mandala and named for the Tamil months.

puducherry.name: Puducherry
puducherry.note: A French colonial grid split by a canal into the French and Tamil quarters, along the Bay of Bengal.

jodhpur.name: Jodhpur
jodhpur.note: The blue city's lanes spread below the Mehrangarh fort on its rock ridge.

agra.name: Agra
agra.note: Taj Ganj, the market town that grew up for the Taj Mahal's builders, sits between the mausoleum and the city.

kochi.name: Kochi
kochi.note: Fort Kochi, shaped by Portuguese, Dutch and British rule in turn, on a sandy point at the harbour mouth.

mysuru.name: Mysuru
mysuru.note: Broad avenues and circles planned by the Wodeyar kings radiate around the Mysore Palace.

shimla.name: Shimla
shimla.note: The British summer capital clings to a ridge, its streets running along the contours of the hills.

bhubaneswar.name: Bhubaneswar
bhubaneswar.note: Otto Koenigsberger planned the new capital of Odisha in 1948 as neighbourhood units between wide avenues.

jaisalmer.name: Jaisalmer
jaisalmer.note: A living fort of yellow sandstone on a hill in the Thar desert, with the town packed around it.

male.name: Malé
male.note: One of the most densely built capitals in the world, filling its whole coral island to the seawall.

bhaktapur.name: Bhaktapur
bhaktapur.note: A Newar city of brick courtyards and temple squares, laid out along an old trade route.

galle.name: Galle
galle.note: A Dutch walled grid of 1663 filling a rocky peninsula on the Indian Ocean.

damascus.name: Damascus
damascus.note: The Straight Street of the Roman grid survives inside the walled old city, around the Umayyad Mosque.

aleppo.name: Aleppo
aleppo.note: The covered souks of the old city lead to the citadel on its great mound.

sanaa.name: Sanaa
sanaa.note: Tower houses of rammed earth and burnt brick crowd the walled old city, with gardens between them.

doha.name: Doha
doha.note: The rebuilt Souq Waqif and Msheireb sit by the crescent Corniche of Doha Bay.

amman.name: Amman
amman.note: The downtown fills a valley floor; the rest of the city climbs the steep jabals around it.

tbilisi.name: Tbilisi
tbilisi.note: The old town squeezes into a gorge of the Mtkvari river below the Narikala fortress.

baku.name: Baku
baku.note: The walled Icherisheher sits inside a ring of oil-boom boulevards on the Caspian shore.

yerevan.name: Yerevan
yerevan.note: Alexander Tamanyan's 1924 plan wraps the centre in a ring park, with radial streets.

bukhara.name: Bukhara
bukhara.note: A Silk Road city of domed bazaars, madrasas and the Lyab-i Hauz pool.

khiva.name: Khiva
khiva.note: The Itchan Kala, a rectangular walled inner town of mud brick, survives almost whole.

kashgar.name: Kashgar
kashgar.note: A Uyghur oasis city of mud-brick lanes around the Id Kah Mosque, on the edge of the Taklamakan.

herat.name: Herat
herat.note: An ancient square walled city, divided into quarters by two crossing bazaar streets.

xian.name: Xi'an
xian.note: The Ming city wall encloses a grid centred on the Bell Tower, on the site of the Tang capital Chang'an.

pingyao.name: Pingyao
pingyao.note: One of the best-preserved walled towns in China, its Ming and Qing streets intact.

suzhou.name: Suzhou

lhasa.name: Lhasa

macau.name: Macau
macau.note: Portuguese squares and lanes run up the hills of the peninsula between casinos on reclaimed land.

hiroshima.name: Hiroshima

hoian.name: Hội An

hue.name: Huế

mandalay.name: Mandalay

yangon.name: Yangon

phnompenh.name: Phnom Penh
phnompenh.note: A French colonial grid beside the meeting of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers.

chiangmai.name: Chiang Mai

luangprabang.name: Luang Prabang

georgetown.name: George Town

malacca.name: Malacca

bandung.name: Bandung

semarang.name: Semarang

timbuktu.name: Timbuktu

djenne.name: Djenné

kano.name: Kano

gondar.name: Gondar

lamu.name: Lamu

mombasa.name: Mombasa
mombasa.note: The Swahili old town by Fort Jesus faces the harbour of an island city.

daressalaam.name: Dar es Salaam

kampala.name: Kampala
kampala.note: A city built on hills, with roads winding along the slopes between them.

kigali.name: Kigali
kigali.note: A city of ridges and valleys, its roads following the hilltops.

maputo.name: Maputo

luanda.name: Luanda

antananarivo.name: Antananarivo

tangier.name: Tangier

chefchaouen.name: Chefchaouen

rabat.name: Rabat
rabat.note: The medina and the Kasbah of the Udayas sit at the river mouth, beside a French ville nouvelle.

kairouan.name: Kairouan

tripoli.name: Tripoli

saintlouis.name: Saint-Louis

abidjan.name: Abidjan
abidjan.note: The Plateau business district on a point of the Ébrié Lagoon.

agadez.name: Agadez

oaxaca.name: Oaxaca

puebla.name: Puebla

guanajuato.name: Guanajuato

antigua.name: Antigua Guatemala

merida.name: Mérida
merida.note: A strict numbered grid laid over the Maya city of T'ho in 1542: even streets run north–south.

campeche.name: Campeche
campeche.note: A colonial grid enclosed by a hexagonal wall built against pirates.

lapaz.name: La Paz
lapaz.note: A colonial grid poured into a deep canyon, with streets climbing hundreds of metres to the altiplano.

potosi.name: Potosí
potosi.note: A silver-rush city at 4,000 m below the Cerro Rico, once among the largest cities in the world.

salvador.name: Salvador
salvador.note: An upper and a lower city split by an escarpment above the Bay of All Saints.

ouropreto.name: Ouro Preto
ouropreto.note: A gold-rush town of steep lanes strung along the ridges and valleys of the hills.

valparaiso.name: Valparaíso
valparaiso.note: A narrow port strip below dozens of steep hills, linked by funiculars and stairways.

medellin.name: Medellín
medellin.note: A grid on the floor of the Aburrá valley, with the city climbing the slopes on both sides.

santodomingo.name: Santo Domingo
santodomingo.note: The Ciudad Colonial is the first European town in the Americas laid out on a grid, from 1502.

sanjuan.name: San Juan
sanjuan.note: Old San Juan's walled grid sits at the tip of an islet between the Atlantic and the bay.

panamacity.name: Panama City
panamacity.note: Casco Viejo, the walled grid of 1673 on a small peninsula, faces the towers across the bay.

portauprince.name: Port-au-Prince
portauprince.note: A French colonial grid by the bay, climbing toward the hills behind.

benghazi.name: Benghazi
benghazi.note: Italian colonial streets of the 1920s and 30s meet the old souq quarter by the harbour, with the lagoon of 23 July Lake to the north-east.

dubrovnik.name: Dubrovnik
dubrovnik.note: A walled town on a rocky promontory: the straight Stradun runs along an old filled-in channel, with stepped lanes climbing either side inside the ring of walls.

tallinn.name: Tallinn
tallinn.note: A Hanseatic lower town and the Toompea hill castle above it, still inside medieval walls and towers, wrapped by a green belt where the bastions stood.

vilnius.name: Vilnius
vilnius.note: One of Europe's largest surviving old towns: crooked baroque streets fan out from the cathedral and castle hill where the Vilnia meets the Neris.

ljubljana.name: Ljubljana
ljubljana.note: The old town is squeezed into a strip between castle hill and a bend of the Ljubljanica, stitched together by Jože Plečnik's bridges and riverside terraces.

sarajevo.name: Sarajevo
sarajevo.note: A long, narrow valley city: the Ottoman bazaar of Baščaršija at the east end gives way to Austro-Hungarian blocks along the Miljacka river.

kotor.name: Kotor
kotor.note: A tiny triangular walled town wedged between the inner Bay of Kotor and a sheer mountainside, its fortress walls zigzagging up the cliff behind.

sofia.name: Sofia
sofia.note: Roman Serdica lies under the Largo, a 1950s socialist-classical ensemble of three grand blocks, ringed by yellow-paved boulevards and church domes.

minsk.name: Minsk
minsk.note: Almost destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt along Independence Avenue, a Stalinist boulevard of palatial blocks and huge squares.

luxembourg.name: Luxembourg
luxembourg.note: A fortress city on a rock plateau, cut off on two sides by the deep Pétrusse and Alzette gorges, with the old town on top and the Grund down in the valley.

monaco.name: Monaco
monaco.note: A sliver of coast packed with towers: the palace on its rock, the harbour below, and terraces of apartments climbing to the French border.

riyadh.name: Riyadh
riyadh.note: A car city on a vast superblock grid of walled villas, split by the King Fahd Road spine of towers.

jeddah.name: Jeddah
jeddah.note: Al-Balad, the old port town of coral-stone tower houses with wooden lattice balconies, now hemmed in by wide modern roads.

baghdad.name: Baghdad
baghdad.note: Rusafa's old souks and lanes on the east bank of a wide bend in the Tigris, crossed by bridges to the Karkh side.

muscat.name: Muscat
muscat.note: Low white houses squeezed into coves between bare, jagged mountains and the sea, strung along the Mutrah corniche.

kuwaitcity.name: Kuwait City
kuwaitcity.note: The First Ring Road follows the line of the old mud wall; inside, the old town was cleared for towers and the grand mosque, with rings of suburbs beyond.

ashgabat.name: Ashgabat
ashgabat.note: Rebuilt after the 1948 earthquake and later clad in white marble: huge monuments, palaces and fountains set along empty boulevards.

bishkek.name: Bishkek
bishkek.note: A Soviet-planned grid of tree-lined avenues and irrigation channels around Ala-Too Square, with the mountains always to the south.

kinshasa.name: Kinshasa
kinshasa.note: Gombe, the Belgian colonial centre, lies on a grid beside the Congo River, facing Brazzaville across the water.

harare.name: Harare
harare.note: Founded as Fort Salisbury in 1890 and laid out as a rigid grid of very wide streets.

windhoek.name: Windhoek
windhoek.note: A small German colonial centre of the 1890s strung along Independence Avenue, with the Christuskirche and Tintenpalast on the slope above.

mogadishu.name: Mogadishu
mogadishu.note: Hamar Weyne and Shangani, the old coral-stone quarters, sit on the Indian Ocean shore beside the Italian colonial centre.

nouakchott.name: Nouakchott
nouakchott.note: Built from scratch from 1958 as Mauritania's new capital on open dunes near the Atlantic: a sandy grid of low buildings and wide avenues.

cotonou.name: Cotonou
cotonou.note: The city is split by the channel joining Lake Nokoué to the sea, with the vast Dantokpa market on its bank.

ouagadougou.name: Ouagadougou
ouagadougou.note: A French colonial grid with diagonal avenues meeting at big roundabouts such as the Place des Nations Unies.

asuncion.name: Asunción
asuncion.note: One of South America's oldest cities: a Spanish grid on a bluff above a bay of the Paraguay River.

georgetowngy.name: Georgetown
georgetowngy.note: A Dutch-then-British grid below sea level, behind a sea wall and laced with drainage canals, with wide avenues on filled-in canals.

paramaribo.name: Paramaribo
paramaribo.note: A Dutch colonial town of white wooden houses on a grid along the Suriname River, beside Fort Zeelandia.

kingston.name: Kingston
kingston.note: Laid out in 1692 after an earthquake destroyed Port Royal: a grid running up from the harbour to the Parade.

sanjose.name: San José
sanjose.note: A Spanish grid of numbered avenidas and calles in a highland valley; locals give directions by landmarks, not street names.

granada.name: Granada
granada.note: One of the first Spanish towns on the American mainland: a grid of colourful single-storey houses running from the cathedral square down to Lake Nicaragua.

lasvegas.name: Las Vegas
lasvegas.note: The Strip: giant casino resorts and their car parks lined up along Las Vegas Boulevard.

thimphu.name: Thimphu
thimphu.note: A small capital strung along a steep river valley, every building in traditional Bhutanese style, and no traffic lights.

bandarseribegawan.name: Bandar Seri Begawan
bandarseribegawan.note: Kampong Ayer, a water village of stilt houses and boardwalks across the Brunei River from the golden-domed mosque.

suva.name: Suva
suva.note: A small colonial port on a hilly peninsula between the harbour and Laucala Bay.

bern.name: Bern
bern.note: The old town fills a tight loop of the Aare: three long arcaded streets run down the spine of the peninsula to the bear pit bridge.

toledo.name: Toledo
toledo.note: A hilltop maze of Moorish, Jewish and Christian lanes, wrapped on three sides by the gorge of the Tagus.

salzburg.name: Salzburg
salzburg.note: The baroque old town is squeezed between the Salzach and the Mönchsberg cliff, with the Hohensalzburg fortress on the hill above.

siena.name: Siena
siena.note: Three ridgetop streets meet at the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo, where the Palio is run.

bruges.name: Bruges
bruges.note: An egg-shaped ring canal follows the old walls around a medieval core of canals, squares and the belfry.

strasbourg.name: Strasbourg
strasbourg.note: The Grande Île, the old town around the cathedral, is an island ringed by two arms of the Ill, with the half-timbered Petite France at its tip.

granadaes.name: Granada
granadaes.note: The Alhambra palace on its wooded ridge faces the white Moorish lanes of the Albaicín across the Darro valley.

split.name: Split
split.note: The old town grew inside the walls of Diocletian's Roman palace, a rectangle on the harbour front.

genoa.name: Genoa
genoa.note: One of Europe's densest old towns: a tangle of narrow caruggi pressed between the old port and steep hills.

nice.name: Nice
nice.note: The Promenade des Anglais curves along the Baie des Anges to the old town under castle hill, with the port beyond.

sansebastian.name: San Sebastián
sansebastian.note: La Concha, a shell-shaped bay between two hills, with the old town at its neck and a 19th-century grid behind the beach.

bilbao.name: Bilbao
bilbao.note: The Nervión winds past the old Siete Calles, the 19th-century Ensanche grid and the titanium curves of the Guggenheim.

bergen.name: Bergen
bergen.note: The Vågen harbour inlet with the Hanseatic wharf of Bryggen along one side, between seven steep hills.

bath.name: Bath
bath.note: Georgian set pieces in honey stone: the round Circus and the great sweep of the Royal Crescent above the Roman baths and the Avon.

oxford.name: Oxford
oxford.note: College quadrangles packed into a medieval street plan around Carfax, between the Cherwell and the Thames.

cambridge.name: Cambridge
cambridge.note: Colleges line the Cam, their lawns running down to the river along the Backs.

york.name: York
york.note: The medieval walls still circle much of the old city, around the Minster and the crooked Shambles, where the Foss meets the Ouse.

liverpool.name: Liverpool
liverpool.note: The Pier Head and a line of docks along the Mersey, the old port's warehouses and the commercial centre climbing behind.

cologne.name: Cologne
cologne.note: A half-circle of boulevards, the Ring, follows the medieval wall around the old town, which faces the Rhine and the cathedral.

dresden.name: Dresden
dresden.note: The rebuilt baroque Altstadt of the Frauenkirche and the Zwinger lines a bend of the Elbe, with its broad meadows left unbuilt.

heidelberg.name: Heidelberg
heidelberg.note: The old town is one long strip between the Neckar and a wooded hillside, with the ruined castle above.

geneva.name: Geneva
geneva.note: The Rhône leaves the lake through the middle of town, with the old town on its hill on the south bank.

rotterdam.name: Rotterdam
rotterdam.note: Bombed flat in 1940 and rebuilt as a modern city of towers, with the Erasmus Bridge across the Nieuwe Maas.

bologna.name: Bologna
bologna.note: Arcaded streets radiate from the Piazza Maggiore and its leaning towers to a ring of boulevards on the line of the last walls.

pisa.name: Pisa
pisa.note: The old town lines a bend of the Arno; in its walled north-west corner the cathedral, baptistery and Leaning Tower stand on a lawn.

cordoba.name: Córdoba
cordoba.note: The great Mezquita, a huge square mosque-cathedral, sits beside the Guadalquivir among the whitewashed lanes of the Judería.

avignon.name: Avignon
avignon.note: Complete 14th-century walls ring the town of the popes, with the Palais des Papes and the broken bridge on the Rhône.

palermo.name: Palermo
palermo.note: Two straight streets cross at the Quattro Canti, cutting a maze of Arab-Norman lanes into four quarters near the port.

pittsburgh.name: Pittsburgh
pittsburgh.note: Downtown, the Golden Triangle, fills the point where the Allegheny and Monongahela meet to form the Ohio, ringed by bridges.

sandiego.name: San Diego
sandiego.note: A downtown grid and the Gaslamp Quarter on the bay, with the convention centre and marinas along the waterfront.

charleston.name: Charleston
charleston.note: A colonial grid on a narrow peninsula between the Ashley and Cooper rivers, ending at the Battery.

annapolis.name: Annapolis
annapolis.note: A 1695 baroque plan: streets radiate from two circles, one around the State House and one around the church, down to the harbour.

stlouis.name: St. Louis
stlouis.note: A riverfront grid on the Mississippi, with the Gateway Arch in its park on the levee.

ottawa.name: Ottawa
ottawa.note: Parliament Hill on its bluff above the Ottawa River, with the Rideau Canal locks stepping down beside it.

manaus.name: Manaus
manaus.note: A rubber-boom port on the Rio Negro deep in the Amazon, with the domed opera house above the floating docks.

recife.name: Recife
recife.note: Built on islands and peninsulas where two rivers meet the sea, joined by many bridges, behind the reef that gave the city its name.

mendoza.name: Mendoza
mendoza.note: Rebuilt after the 1861 earthquake as a wide grid with a large central square and four smaller squares around it, its streets lined with irrigation ditches.

hangzhou.name: Hangzhou
hangzhou.note: The city lines the east shore of West Lake, with its causeways, islands and wooded hills on the other three sides.

chongqing.name: Chongqing
chongqing.note: Towers crowd the hilly Yuzhong peninsula at the meeting of the Yangtze and the Jialing.

busan.name: Busan
busan.note: A port of steep hillside neighbourhoods wrapped around the harbour, with Yeongdo island across the channel.

nagasaki.name: Nagasaki
nagasaki.note: A narrow harbour between steep hills; the fan-shaped Dejima island where Dutch traders were kept still shows in the street plan.

abudhabi.name: Abu Dhabi
abudhabi.note: A planned superblock grid of towers on an island, laid out after oil in the 1960s, with the Corniche along the Gulf.

mecca.name: Mecca
mecca.note: The Masjid al-Haram around the Kaaba fills the valley floor, ringed by giant hotel towers and the Abraj Al Bait clock tower.

luxor.name: Luxor
luxor.note: Ancient Thebes: Luxor Temple stands on the Nile corniche, linked to Karnak by an avenue of sphinxes.

durban.name: Durban
durban.note: A grid between the beachfront Golden Mile on the Indian Ocean and the big natural harbour behind its sandspit.

goldcoast.name: Gold Coast
goldcoast.note: Surfers Paradise: a strip of towers between the surf beach and the Nerang River's canal estates.

london-city.name: London
london-city.note: The Square Mile: the Roman and medieval City’s crooked lanes, now crowded with towers, between St Paul’s and the Tower of London by Tower Bridge.

london-docklands.name: London
london-docklands.note: Canary Wharf’s towers rise from the old West India Docks on the Isle of Dogs, inside a tight loop of the Thames.

newyork-lower.name: New York
newyork-lower.note: New Amsterdam’s crooked streets survive below Wall Street at the tip of Manhattan, where the 1811 grid had not yet begun.

newyork-centralpark.name: New York
newyork-centralpark.note: The grid stops for Central Park, cut out of the 1811 plan, with Fifth Avenue’s mansions and the Metropolitan Museum along its east side.
newyork-centralpark.area: Central Park and the Upper East Side

paris-cite.name: Paris
paris-cite.note: The medieval heart of Paris on the Seine’s two islands, with Notre-Dame, and the Marais’s old lanes on the Right Bank.
paris-cite.area: Île de la Cité and the Marais

paris-champdemars.name: Paris
paris-champdemars.note: Two great axes on the Left Bank: the Champ de Mars from the Eiffel Tower to the École Militaire, and the Esplanade des Invalides.
paris-champdemars.area: Champ de Mars and Les Invalides

tokyo-shinjuku.name: Tokyo
tokyo-shinjuku.note: West Shinjuku’s planned skyscraper district beside one of the world’s busiest stations, with the gardens of Shinjuku Gyoen to the south-east.

tokyo-asakusa.name: Tokyo
tokyo-asakusa.note: The old low city: Sensō-ji temple and its shopping lanes beside the Sumida River, with the Skytree across the water.

rome-vatican.name: Rome
rome-vatican.note: Bernini’s colonnade embraces St Peter’s Square; the Vatican’s walls enclose the gardens behind the basilica, and Via della Conciliazione runs to the Tiber.

rome-colosseum.name: Rome
rome-colosseum.note: The oval of the Colosseum and the Roman Forum below the Palatine, with the long Circus Maximus to the south and Via dei Fori Imperiali cut straight through.

istanbul-beyoglu.name: Istanbul
istanbul-beyoglu.note: Across the Golden Horn from the old city: the Genoese Galata Tower and the steep lanes climbing to İstiklal Avenue.

istanbul-kadikoy.name: Istanbul
istanbul-kadikoy.note: On the Asian shore, the ferry port of Kadıköy and the old Haydarpaşa station face the historic peninsula across the mouth of the Bosphorus.

beijing-templeofheaven.name: Beijing
beijing-templeofheaven.note: The walled park of the Temple of Heaven, its northern corners rounded for heaven and its southern ones square for earth, beside the old Qianmen quarter.

beijing-houhai.name: Beijing
beijing-houhai.note: The Shichahai lakes and the hutong lanes of the old Inner City north of the Forbidden City, with the Drum and Bell Towers.

shanghai-lujiazui.name: Shanghai
shanghai-lujiazui.note: Pudong’s towers – the Oriental Pearl, Jin Mao, the World Financial Center and the Shanghai Tower – on a bend of the Huangpu facing the Bund.

shanghai-frenchconcession.name: Shanghai
shanghai-frenchconcession.note: Plane-tree-lined streets and lilong lane houses of the old French Concession, laid out between the wars.

dubai-downtown.name: Dubai
dubai-downtown.note: The Burj Khalifa and the Dubai Mall beside a man-made lake, with the towers of Sheikh Zayed Road alongside.

dubai-palm.name: Dubai
dubai-palm.note: A man-made island shaped like a palm tree, each frond lined with villas and private beaches.

hongkong-kowloon.name: Hong Kong
hongkong-kowloon.note: The tip of the Kowloon peninsula: the Star Ferry pier, Nathan Road heading north, and the harbour front facing Hong Kong Island.

singapore-kampongglam.name: Singapore
singapore-kampongglam.note: The quarters of Raffles’s town plan: the Sultan Mosque in Kampong Glam and the shophouse streets of Little India.

chicago-navypier.name: Chicago
chicago-navypier.note: Navy Pier juts a kilometre into Lake Michigan from Streeterville, land made from fill along the lakeshore.

sydney-bondi.name: Sydney
sydney-bondi.note: The crescent of Bondi Beach between two sandstone headlands, its streets climbing the slopes behind.

mumbai-marinedrive.name: Mumbai
mumbai-marinedrive.note: The Queen’s Necklace: Marine Drive’s Art Deco apartments curve around Back Bay towards Malabar Hill.

madrid-retiro.name: Madrid
madrid-retiro.note: The Retiro park with its great pond, and the Paseo del Prado’s museums, on the eastern edge of the old city.

moscow-city.name: Moscow
moscow-city.note: The glass towers of the Moscow International Business Centre on a bend of the Moskva, among older housing blocks.

barcelona-barceloneta.name: Barcelona
barcelona-barceloneta.note: The 18th-century Barceloneta, a triangle of long, narrow blocks between the old port and the beach.

berlin-alexanderplatz.name: Berlin
berlin-alexanderplatz.note: East Berlin’s showpiece: the TV tower at Alexanderplatz and the broad Karl-Marx-Allee lined with Stalin-era blocks.

washington-capitol.name: Washington
washington-capitol.note: The Capitol crowns L’Enfant’s plan: avenues radiate from it and the National Mall stretches west.

mexicocity-reforma.name: Mexico City
mexicocity-reforma.note: Paseo de la Reforma, laid out under Emperor Maximilian, slices diagonally through the grid with its glorietas and the Angel of Independence.

saopaulo-paulista.name: São Paulo
saopaulo-paulista.note: Avenida Paulista runs along a ridge lined with banks and towers, with MASP’s gallery raised over its own plaza.

rio-ipanema.name: Rio de Janeiro
rio-ipanema.note: Ipanema’s grid on a sandbar between the Atlantic and the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon.

buenosaires-puertomadero.name: Buenos Aires
buenosaires-puertomadero.note: The brick warehouses and new towers of Puerto Madero line four long docks between the old centre and the river reserve.

cairo-islamic.name: Cairo
cairo-islamic.note: The medieval Fatimid city: the Khan el-Khalili bazaar, al-Azhar and the mosques of al-Muizz Street, packed with lanes.

bangkok-lumphini.name: Bangkok
bangkok-lumphini.note: Lumphini Park’s lakes and lawns beside the towers of Silom and Sathorn, Bangkok’s business district.

seoul-yeouido.name: Seoul
seoul-yeouido.note: An island in the Han River turned into Seoul’s financial district, with the National Assembly at its western end.

vienna-schonbrunn.name: Vienna
vienna-schonbrunn.note: The Habsburg summer palace and its baroque gardens, with avenues fanning out uphill to the Gloriette.

stpetersburg-vasilyevsky.name: Saint Petersburg
stpetersburg-vasilyevsky.note: Vasilyevsky Island’s numbered “lines”, laid out by Peter the Great as streets meant to be canals, up to the Spit facing the Winter Palace.

taipei-xinyi.name: Taipei
taipei-xinyi.note: Xinyi’s planned superblocks around Taipei 101, at the foot of the hills on the city’s east side.

kualalumpur-klcc.name: Kuala Lumpur
kualalumpur-klcc.note: The twin Petronas Towers and the KLCC park in the Golden Triangle, on the site of the old Selangor Turf Club.

capetown-waterfront.name: Cape Town
capetown-waterfront.note: The Victorian harbour basins turned into the V&A Waterfront, with Green Point’s stadium and the Atlantic beyond.

lima-miraflores.name: Lima
lima-miraflores.note: Miraflores sits on clifftops above the Pacific, its streets ending at the Malecón with the Costa Verde far below.

osaka-castle.name: Osaka
osaka-castle.note: Osaka Castle on its stone platform inside two rings of moats, ringed by park and the Osaka Business Park’s towers.

boston-backbay.name: Boston
boston-backbay.note: Back Bay was a tidal marsh, filled in the 19th century and laid out as a French-style grid of brownstones along Commonwealth Avenue.

newdelhi-old.name: New Delhi
newdelhi-old.note: Shahjahanabad, the walled Mughal city: the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid and the crowded lanes off Chandni Chowk.

losangeles-venice.name: Los Angeles
losangeles-venice.note: Abbot Kinney’s 1905 “Venice of America”: canals and walk streets behind the beach, now part of Los Angeles.
